skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Docker workflow guidance for multi-stage builds, Docker Compose orchestration, image optimization, debugging, and production container practices.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through practical Docker builds, Compose stacks, debugging, and production hardening.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate Docker workflow documentation, and many static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, ignore patterns, and Docker templates. Confirmed concerns include hardcoded development credentials, a public connectivity probe, and helper commands that can expose or delete Docker data. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded example credentials in Compose files
remediation.suggestion: Replace default passwords and admin accounts with placeholders, secret references, and clear production warnings.

remediation.issue: Container environment variables can be printed without redaction
remediation.suggestion: Redact names containing SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, KEY, and CREDENTIAL before displaying environment output.

remediation.issue: Docker cleanup removes resources with forced prune commands
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation prompt and document that unused volumes may contain persistent data.

remediation.issue: Connectivity check uses a fixed public IP address
remediation.suggestion: Make the connectivity target configurable and prefer an internal endpoint for private environments.

semantic_findings.title: Default Credentials in Docker Compose Examples
semantic_findings.description: The Compose template includes hardcoded database, Redis, RabbitMQ, and Grafana credentials. Users could copy these defaults into shared or production environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credentials are directly visible in reusable Compose examples. The file is educational, but the values are unsafe if copied without replacement.

semantic_findings.title: Container Environment Disclosure Helper
semantic_findings.description: The helper script has an env command that prints all environment variables from a running container. This can expose secrets in terminal output or support logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The show_env function directly runs env inside the target container and sorts the output. No redaction is present before printing values.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Docker Cleanup Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup helper prunes stopped containers, dangling images, unused volumes, and unused networks with forced flags. This can delete Docker data unexpectedly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cleanup function invokes multiple Docker prune commands with -f. This is intentional automation, but it lacks an extra confirmation step.

content.user_title: Build Docker Workflows With AI Guidance
content.value_statement: Docker setup is slow when teams need secure images, Compose stacks, and repeatable debugging. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical container workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates .dockerignore guidance for smaller, safer build contexts.
Explains multi-stage Dockerfiles for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust.
Drafts Docker Compose services with networks, volumes, health checks, and dependencies.
Provides Docker debugging commands for logs, shells, ports, stats, and health checks.
Suggests image optimization steps using layer caching, BuildKit, and smaller base images.
Outlines production practices such as non-root users, health checks, and vulnerability scanning.
limitations: Does not run Docker commands unless the user executes supplied scripts or commands.
Example credentials and service names must be replaced before production use.
Generated Dockerfiles still require project-specific package files and entry points.
Helper scripts can expose container environment variables during debugging.

use_cases.title: Containerize a Web App
use_cases.description: Create a Dockerfile and Compose stack for a frontend, backend, database, and cache.

use_cases.title: Optimize Existing Images
use_cases.description: Reduce image size by reviewing layers, build cache order, base images, and ignored files.

use_cases.title: Debug Container Issues
use_cases.description: Investigate failing health checks, logs, ports, volumes, networks, and resource usage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my project structure and draft a multi-stage Dockerfile. Explain each stage and list files I must provide.

prompt_templates.title: Add Compose Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Docker Compose setup for my app, database, cache, and worker. Include networks, volumes, dependencies, and health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Docker workflow to diagnose this container problem. Check logs, ports, health, mounts, and networking before suggesting fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Dockerfile and Compose files for production readiness. Focus on secrets, users, image versions, health checks, and build size.

output_examples.input: A Node.js API needs smaller images and a production run path.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering dependency caching, a non-root runtime user, health checks, and final image size checks.

output_examples.input: A Compose stack has a backend, database, Redis cache, and background worker.
output_examples.output: A service design with private networks, named volumes, health-based dependencies, and warnings about replacing default secrets.

output_examples.input: A container starts, fails its health check, and exposes no useful logs.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for health status, recent logs, port mappings, shell access, DNS checks, and volume permissions.

best_practices: Replace all example passwords, keys, and admin accounts before deployment.
Review helper script commands before running them on shared Docker hosts.
Use pinned image versions, non-root users, health checks, and vulnerability scans.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example Compose credentials into production environments.
Do not print container environment variables in shared logs or support tickets.
Do not run Docker cleanup commands on hosts with unknown volume ownership.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scripts. Commands run only when the user executes them.

faq.question: Can it create production Dockerfiles?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft production patterns, but users must adapt paths, commands, ports, and secrets.

faq.question: Does it support Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers services, networks, volumes, health checks, dependencies, and environment-specific overrides.

faq.question: Is the helper script safe to run anywhere?
faq.answer: No. It can inspect containers, print environment variables, and prune Docker resources.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill metadata supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing outputs?
faq.answer: Review secrets, default passwords, exposed ports, volume mounts, image tags, and destructive cleanup commands.
